drivingQuestion: Is even her own maidservant believed to testify she was not defiled?
outcomeNote: the contradiction is raised here; its resolution lies beyond this unit

segments.he: אִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים, אֲפִילּוּ עֶבֶד וַאֲפִילּוּ שִׁפְחָה נֶאֱמָנִין. וַאֲפִילּוּ שִׁפְחָה דִּידַהּ מְהֵימְנָא? וּרְמִינְהִי: לֹא תִּתְיַיחֵד עִמּוֹ אֶלָּא עַל פִּי עֵדִים.
segments.en: § We learned in the mishna: «If» they «have witnesses, even» if the witness is «a slave and even» if the witness is «a maidservant, they are deemed credible.» The Gemara asks: «And» is «even her» personal «maidservant deemed credible?» The Gemara «raises a contradiction» from a mishna (Gittin 73a): With regard to one who divorced his wife conditionally, and the condition was not yet fulfilled, the woman «may enter into seclusion with him only on the basis of» the presence of «witnesses,» due to the concern that they will engage in intercourse. If between the drafting of a bill of divorce and its taking effect the husband and wife enter into seclusion together, the bill of divorce must be discarded and a new document drafted in its place.
